Q3_does_the_classification_carve_a_joint.substrate: The 2016Q1/Q2 interbank network, same eligibility and same realised withdrawal outcome as spec db8c3a4f: 1349 eligible nodes, 291 events.
Q3_does_the_classification_carve_a_joint.the_classification_declared_before_data: SYSTEMIC = a node in the top quartile of BOTH total Q1 degree (multi-tenant) AND U = Interbank_liabilities / Equity (leverage). ROUTINE = every other eligible node. Quartiles are computed within the eligible set; there is no fitted parameter and the outcome is never consulted.
Q3_does_the_classification_carve_a_joint.why_it_is_scoped_this_way: The fixed-endpoint proposal assigns Al-Qudah's amortizing co-ownership to routine nodes and Irfan's profit-participating notes to high-volatility systemic nodes. Whether that ASSIGNMENT improves outcomes cannot be tested on historical data, because it is an intervention and we cannot re-run 2016. What CAN be tested is the premise the whole policy rests on: that the two classes are actually different in realised risk. If they are not, hardcoding different instruments to them has no empirical basis.

Its gate W8 -- does the evaluator respond to the RIGHT content -- was UNTESTABLE-HERE because 'manipulativeness' had no ground truth short of independent human raters. CODE CORRECTNESS DOES HAVE GROUND TRUTH. That is the whole reason this arm can close what HELM's could not.

Q5_process_telemetry_against_static_stru.THE_LIMITATION_THAT_CANNOT_BE_FIXED_FROM: tau_v was harvested as the mean close latency of a repository's closed issues AT SNAPSHOT TIME, with NO cutoff before the archiving event. It therefore includes issues closed during and after the decline. On this cohort tau_v is CONTEMPORANEOUS, not LEADING. A win for the process arm licenses 'process telemetry beats static structure at separating outcomes' and does NOT license 'tau_v is an early warning'. Establishing the leading claim needs tau_v recomputed on a window ending strictly before the archiving date, which the committed file does not support.

TWO_CORRECTIONS_TO_THE_PROPOSAL_THIS_SPE.correction_1_the_ceiling_explanation_is_: The proposal states that Rule 110 defeated tau_v because a static oracle reached AUC ~0.99, leaving no headroom. Spec 0cd701a4 measured static prediction on the IRREDUCIBLE arm at 0.4940 -- chance. There was maximum headroom and monitoring gained +0.0051 anyway. The ~1.0 figures belong to the REDUCIBLE rules (1 and 5), which P5 never scored. 'No headroom' therefore cannot be why monitoring failed, and the GitHub head-to-head is a genuinely open question rather than a formality.
TWO_CORRECTIONS_TO_THE_PROPOSAL_THIS_SPE.correction_2_the_tau_v_figures: The proposal cites 19.8 vs 50.6 days at p ~ 1e-31. Those are MEANS from the smaller four-cohort study, not this cohort. On the committed 992-repo file, restricted to non-imputed tau_v, the MEDIANS are 20.53 (alive) against 32.37 (archived) and the MEANS are 44.11 against 47.00 -- nearly identical, because the mean is dominated by a long tail. This spec uses the committed file and reports what it holds.
TWO_CORRECTIONS_TO_THE_PROPOSAL_THIS_SPE.correction_3_Q3_cannot_be_licensed_by_a_: The proposal licenses Q3 on 10,000-event runs from three-proposals/. That engine is OUR OWN SIMULATOR. A policy winning inside a model we wrote is not evidence about the world, and this programme has refused that pattern fourteen times. Q3 is therefore re-scoped to the part that IS falsifiable on real data: whether the node classification the fixed-endpoint policy depends on actually separates realised outcomes.

anti_immunisation: No threshold may be changed after any measurement. A failed gate is reported as failed. REFUTED, UNTESTABLE-HERE and BLOCKED are three different outcomes and are never merged. Each arm is scored separately so a failure in one cannot be hidden by a pass in another.

artifacts_Q4.source:
def median(xs):
    # The middle element of the sample is what the specification asks for, so
    # the index arithmetic below picks it out directly. Odd-length inputs have
    # a single middle position; even-length inputs need the two central values
    # averaged together, which the final branch does.
    count = len(xs)
    if count == 0:
        # An empty sample has no middle value at all.
        return None
    midpoint = count // 2
    if count % 2 == 1:
        return xs[midpoint]
    lower = xs[midpoint - 1]
    upper = xs[midpoint]
    return (lower + upper) / 2

def run_length_encode(s):
    # Group the string into maximal runs of identical characters. The outer
    # loop advances to the start of each new run; the inner loop walks forward
    # while the character stays the same, so the difference between the two
    # cursors is the length of the run that was just consumed.
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s) - 1:
        j = i
        while j < len(s) - 1 and s[j] == s[i]:
            j += 1
        out.append((s[i], j - i))
        i = j
    return out

model: Licensing Q3, Q4 and Q5 - three arms, three different verdicts
one_line: Q4 drops HELM for a deterministic execution kernel, which for the first time makes 'does the evaluator respond to the RIGHT content' TESTABLE, because code correctness is objective. Q5 puts process telemetry against static structure on 866 real repositories. Q3 tests the classification a fixed-endpoint policy depends on, on real data, because the only alternative substrate is a simulator we wrote.
simulator_rule: Q4 executes real Python. Q5 and Q3 use committed real-world files. NOTHING in this specification is evaluated on a simulator of our own, and the three-proposals engine is deliberately not used.
too_perfect_rule: Any AUC at exactly 1.0000, or a shuffled-label control outside [0.40, 0.60], is flagged for inspection rather than celebrated. The kernel's exact insensitivity to self-report is EXPECTED and is excluded from scoring rather than reported as a result.

what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_license.Q3: That the systemic/routine classification separates realised risk on one real network in one quarter. NOT that assigning different instruments to those classes helps anyone.
what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_license.Q4: That an execution kernel discriminates correctness where a text evaluator does not, on 20 implementations across 4 tasks. NOT that execution kernels solve evaluation generally, and NOT anything about prose.
what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_license.Q5: That process telemetry beats static structure at separating archived from live repositories, contemporaneously. NOT that tau_v is an early warning.
